game: New York Jets @ Chicago Bears (Sun 1:00 PM ET)
why: Chicago is starting 38-year-old backup Case Keenum, and +3.5 means the Jets still cover with a 3-point loss, which is the most common NFL margin. The market makes this a near coin flip (-110 on both sides, unchanged all week), and the evidence is roughly balanced rather than stacked against New York. It's live, not good: the Jets are missing four offensive starters, so treat it as a coin flip with a backup-QB tailwind.
evidence: Injuries: Bears QB Caleb Williams is out 3-4 weeks (Grade 2 hamstring); Keenum starts (KSL/AP). Jets are without RB Breece Hall, WR Adonai Mitchell, TE Mason Taylor and LG Dylan Parham; rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq is questionable (ESPN, NFL.com).

Player usage: with Hall out, Braelon Allen takes over (19 carries for 61 yards, 3.2 per carry, so far), a role change that lowers the run game. Geno Smith is 75.5% passing with 4 TD, 0 INT in 3 games (Yahoo Sports).

Hot-streak check: Garrett Wilson and Sadiq's 212 yards in Week 3 came against Detroit, the league's worst defense by EPA (Sharp Football). That's matchup-inflated production with no usage data showing a role change, so it gets low weight. Keenum's 247 yards and 2 TDs against a depleted Eagles team is likewise one game.
Efficiency: Jets defense allows 4.8 yards/play vs Chicago's 6.1; Chicago's offense gains 5.9 yards/play to New York's 5.0, mostly with Williams at QB (Sharp Football).
Against: the Jets' line allowed 9 sacks in Weeks 2-3 after 0 in Week 1 (amNY), and Parham's absence doesn't help. Chicago is home off a 27-7 win over Philadelphia.
Line movement: Bears -3.5 on Sept 30 (amNY) and Oct 1 (Covers), still -3.5 now (Odds API). Hall's injury was known all week and didn't move the line.
Analysts: Covers takes Jets +3.5; NFL.com analysts split 3-2 for Chicago outright.
trend: Jets went 3-4-1 ATS as a road underdog in 2025 (8 games, per TeamRankings BetIQ). Small sample — directional only, not a strong signal, and it's a different roster and QB, so it barely applies.

game: Cleveland Browns @ New York Jets (Sun 1:00 PM ET)
why: The Jets only need to win by 2 at home, so this isn't absurd, and the Jets' defense has been respectable (5.0 yards per play allowed). But the offense is last in the league in passing, Breece Hall and Adonai Mitchell are still out, and Cleveland arrives 3-1 with three straight fourth-quarter comebacks. More is working against the Jets than for them.
evidence: Injuries: Breece Hall (quad), Adonai Mitchell (finger), LG Dylan Parham (knee) and CB Jarvis Brownlee (concussion) all DNP Wednesday; TE Mason Taylor full participant. Browns DTs Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr. and G Teven Jenkins DNP (Jets.com, Oct 7).

Player usage: Braelon Allen took 100% of RB carries in Week 4 (14 for 59) with Hall out, a role-driven drop in explosiveness. Garrett Wilson had only 4 targets (26.7% share) for 27 yards because the Jets ran just 32 plays (FFToday; NBC Sports). That's low volume, not a role change.
Efficiency: Jets are 32nd in passing yards and yards per attempt (NBC Sports). Geno Smith has 0 INT and a 109.0 rating but has been sacked 12 times.
Line movement: sources disagree. RotoWire has it opening NYJ -2.5 and moving to -1.5, NBC has -2 to -2.5. Books now sit at -1 to -2.5 (Odds API). No clear signal.
Analysts: SI (Browns +110), NBC (lean Browns +2.5), Covers and DraftKings' expert picks (Browns +2.5) all go against the Jets.

game: New York Jets @ Kansas City Chiefs (Sun 1:00 PM ET)
why: Nine and a half points is a lot to ask a Kansas City team that has lost two straight and is 3-5 ATS. The Jets' offense is a respectable 13th in EPA/play, and SI's writer likes the Jets. But Garrett Wilson, the Jets' leading receiver, is Out with a concussion, the Jets' defense is 21st in EPA, and the total has climbed 4.5 points, which hurts a big underdog. More is working against a cover than for it.
evidence: Injuries: WR Garrett Wilson (concussion; team leader with 43-527-3) is Out, along with S VJ Payne, CB Nahshon Wright, DE Joseph Ossai and LB Trevin Wallace (NFL.com; Fox Sports). Breece Hall (quad) practiced fully Thursday and is trending toward returning after missing five games (TSN; Jets.com).

Usage: Hall's return would be a role-driven boost to the run game after five missed games. Without Wilson, Geno Smith (5th in CPOE, 3 INT, per SI) loses his top target, so it's a role-driven downgrade for the passing game.

Efficiency: Jets offense 13th in EPA/play and 10th in success rate; Jets defense 21st in EPA/play (SI). KC's run game has stalled: Kenneth Walker averaged 2.6 and 3.3 YPC in the two losses (SI). KC is still without CB Mansoor Delane and DTs Peter Woods and Omarr Norman-Lott (NFL.com).
Line movement: KC opened -10 and is now -9.5. The total jumped from 43.5 to 48 (SI opening odds; Odds API), so the market expects more scoring, which usually helps the favorite pull away.
Analysts: SI's writer takes the Jets +9.5. Squawka projects KC 30-13, and Football Nation projects KC 27-20.
trend: KC is 5-3 ATS in the last 8 meetings (8 games, per SI). Small sample, so directional only and not a strong signal. The line likely already reflects it.
